source.title: Efficient Compression of Overparameterized Deep Models through Low-Dimensional Learning Dynamics
source.authors: S. Kwon; Ze-Kai Zhang; Dogyoon Song; Laura Balzano; Qing Qu

record.file_problem: not stated; full paper text supplied
record.tranche_reason: Applies compressed training to nonlinear MLP and ViT classifiers and reports test accuracy; this is a new setting relative to the claim versions. Matrix-recovery experiments do not test the listed natural-label generalization claim.
record.gate_note: The nonlinear classification experiments compare standard networks, networks with an overparameterized penultimate deep linear network (DLN), and compressed DLNs on FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10. Rows below record the reported test-accuracy outcomes. Matrix-recovery recovery-error results and plots of weight-update singular values do not directly test a listed claim version. Results cited from prior work are not extracted as this study's own findings.
record.test_reason: The study tests compression and linear-layer factorization, not any listed claim version. Reporting classifier test accuracy does not establish random-label memorization, generalization beyond an interpolation width, or any of the specified comparisons. Its discussion of overparameterization and implicit bias provides background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that compressing a DLN penultimate layer reduces training time and memory while retaining similar or better classifier accuracy. Their broader contribution concerns low-dimensional learning dynamics and accelerated matrix recovery.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies data-informed spectral initialization and low-rank compression of deep linear layers, including matrix-recovery experiments and nonlinear classifier applications; it does not test the claim's stated interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The nonlinear results differ by architecture and dataset: the compressed model has the highest reported mean accuracy for MLP on FashionMNIST and is close to the DLN variant for ViT on CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: FashionMNIST MLP mean test accuracy is 89.87% for the original, 90.20% with a DLN penultimate layer, and 90.28% with its compressed counterpart. CIFAR-10 ViT means are 84.72%, 84.90%, and 84.89%, respectively, across five runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Factorizing the penultimate layer into a DLN and compressing it can preserve or modestly improve classifier accuracy in these settings.

record.problems: The nonlinear classification accuracy results are from 5 runs; the paper does not state the exact test-set sizes or provide significance tests for these accuracy comparisons. The stated 99% test-accuracy threshold is not reached by every reported model in Table 1, and the table does not clarify how timing and accuracy entries relate for those models.
record.rows_left_out: No matrix-recovery rows were included because recovery error on synthetic matrices, matrix-completion datasets, or MovieLens does not measure the claim's natural-label held-out classification behavior. Figure-only plots of training trajectories and singular values were also outside the listed versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training under the same recipe.
Test-error changes when widening beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All six accuracy values and their reported uncertainties match Table 1. Its claim that timing measures reaching 99% test accuracy is unresolved: every listed accuracy is below 99%. This ambiguity affects timing interpretation, not the transcription of the accuracy values.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep beyond interpolation on natural-label data.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison testing the stated local-connectivity claim.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No batch-size comparison testing a large-batch generalization gap.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of generalization gaps.
No removal of memorized examples or test-accuracy comparison.
